result.title: Beyond the Sink Token: Sink-Guided Key Editing in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: In vision-language models (VLMs), a few sink tokens attract a disproportionate share of attention. While previous studies have examined why these tokens attract attention, we investigate how the sink-key direction affects attention to image and question tokens. Across four probed VLMs, boosting the magnitude of positive sink-aligned components increases attention on average, whereas boosting negative components decreases it; these responses persist through later layers. This identifies the native sink key as a reference for controlling attention beyond its own position. Motivated by this finding, we propose SHRINK, a training-free method that partially reduces sink-aligned components across visible keys during generation. On nine benchmarks under sampled reasoning, it improves mean accuracy by 5.1 and 2.7 percentage points on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-3B, with smaller gains on the other two main models, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Gemma-3-4B. Beyond SHRINK, rescaling sink-aligned key components can replace the attention operations of two existing attention-steering methods, GIFT and ACG, with comparable accuracy on hallucination benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察 VLM 中 sink token 的 sink-key 方向如何调节对图像与问题 token 的注意力，发现放大正向 sink 对齐分量会整体提升注意力、负向则降低，并据此提出免训练的 SHRINK：生成时部分削减可见 key 中与 sink 对齐的分量，在九个基准上带来 2.7–5.1 个百分点左右的平均提升，并可替代 GIFT、ACG 的注意力操作。
AI.relevance_reason: 它把「sink 方向」当作控制视觉证据获取的推理期旋钮，与 LOOK 类行为和注意力结构的分析有直接联系，可供核查其对图像 token 注意与视觉旁路的影响；但评估停留在准确率与幻觉层面，未涉及 latent 推理状态，迁移到 LVR 的具体作用仍需判断。
